newsitem.title: USA: Rockwell to spin off automotive units.
newsitem.headline: Rockwell to spin off automotive units.

text.p: Rockwell International Corp. said Monday that it would spin off its automotive component systems units into a separately traded company as it takes a final step to focus on its world-wide electronics business.
Last December Rockwell completed the sale of its aerospace and defence businesses to Boeing Co. for $3.2 billion.

Rockwell said that as part of the spinoff of the automotive units, which had 1996 sales of $3.1 billion, the company's stockholders would receive shares in the new firm on a pro rata basis, in addition to the stock they hold in Rockwell.
The company said the new shares would be listed on the New York Stock Exchange.
Larry D. Yost, currently president of Rockwell Heavy Vehicle Systems, will become president and chief executive of the new company.

"Today Rockwell is comprised of two distinct businesses -- a group of leading-edge businesses serving segments of the electronics market and automotive component systems, each with significant differences in their markets, products, technologies, investment requirements and strategic growth opportunities," Chairman Donald R. Beall said in a statement.
"After careful consideration of our business options, we're convinced that the full potential of these businesses can best be reached by operating separately," he said.
By spinning off its automotive activities, the company said it completes its transformation to a global electronics firm.

Headquartered in Troy, Mich., Rockwell's Automotive businesses have a worldwide workforce of 16,000, with plants in Iowa, Kentucky, Michigan, Ohio, South Carolina, North Carolina, Tennessee and Wisconsin.
They also have facilities in Australia, Brazil, Canada, China, the Czech Republic, France, Germany, India, Italy, Japan, Korea, Mexico, Spain, Turkey and Britain.
Rockwell said the spinoff is expected to be completed by Sept. 30, the end of its fiscal year.
Rockwell's gained 62.5 cents to $68.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
